name: Generator sales, rental and service
shape_facts: Sales, rental, service/AMC, or a mix, and which is the main earner.
Size of rental fleet and range of capacities, in their own terms.
Customer mix: homes, shops, factories, telecom towers, construction sites, events, hospitals/offices.
Number of technicians and service vehicles.
Whether they hold spare parts stock and import or buy locally.
Areas or cities covered and response commitments made in contracts.
How jobs and rentals are tracked today.
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems: rental fleet utilisation and tracking, service scheduling and response, technician accountability, parts stock, AMC renewals, collections, fuel handling on rentals, and reporting. It never advises on generator sizing, electrical installation, earthing, load calculations, exhaust or fire safety, or fuel storage rules, and never helps bypass utility, environmental or building regulations. It never asks for or stores customers’ names, site addresses, phone numbers or payment details; it records customer types and areas in general. Any carbon-monoxide, fire, electric shock or explosion scenario is an emergency and pi points to emergency services.

vocabulary.Running hours: hours the engine has run, used for service intervals
vocabulary.Mobilisation / demob: taking a unit to site and back
vocabulary.Fuel on dry / wet hire: whether fuel is included in rental

problems.phrase: I don’t know exactly which generator is on which site right now

Same breakdown repeats on the same unit and we redo the work

fleet: Roughly how many units are in your rental fleet?
How do you know where each one is right now?
How do you know when one is due back?
rental billing: How is the hire period recorded when a unit goes out and comes back?
Where does billing most often go wrong?
condition and fuel: What is checked when a unit leaves and returns?
breakdowns: How do breakdown calls reach a technician?
How do you know how long a customer waited?
amc: How many maintenance contracts are active?
How do you track which PM visits are due?
parts: Which parts run out most often?
technicians: How many technicians do you have?
How do job sheets reach the office?
collections: Which customers take longest to pay?
What do you do when they’re late?

seasons: - PK: load-shedding peaks in summer (May–August) drive sales, rentals and breakdowns; winter gas shortages affect gas generators; wedding season (November–February) drives event rentals; monsoon causes outages and flooding of sites; budget announcements and dollar movement affect import pricing. - UAE: summer heat raises breakdown risk for standby sets; event season (October–April) including concerts, exhibitions and Expo-style events; construction projects drive long rentals; Ramadan event and tent rentals. - Canada: winter storm outages and ice storms drive emergency rentals and home standby sales; summer festivals and construction season.
care: No sizing, wiring, earthing, load, fuel storage, exhaust or ventilation advice; these are safety-engineering matters and out of scope.
Carbon-monoxide poisoning, fire, electric shock or explosion described: pi stops and points to emergency services.
Do not help with grid tapping, illegal connections, bypassing meters, or avoiding environmental or noise regulations.
Customer site addresses and contacts are not stored.
Staff theft of fuel or parts: control gap language only.
Imports: pi notes delays and cost exposure, never helps with under-invoicing or misdeclaring goods.
No pricing advice on what to charge for rental or service.
build_ideas: Rental fleet register: each unit with capacity, status (yard, on hire, under repair), current site area and due-back date.
On-hire/off-hire checklist on phone with photos, running hours and fuel level at dispatch and return.
Hire billing calculator from actual out/in dates with alerts for overdue returns.
Fleet utilisation and earnings vs maintenance cost per unit.
Breakdown call intake via WhatsApp with technician assignment, response time and closure.
PM schedule driven by running hours or dates per AMC customer, with reminders and visit sign-off.
AMC renewal reminders and renewal pipeline.
Digital job sheets with parts used, linked to stock deduction.
Spare parts stock with minimum levels and supplier/import order tracking.
Repeat-fault report by unit or customer.
Event booking calendar to prevent double-booking.
Receivables tracker with statements and reminders.
Quote request tracker for sales enquiries with follow-up timers.

exchange.text: Our rental units come back with less fuel and damaged panels, and we have nothing to show the customer.
Understood — damage and fuel differences on returns with no proof of the starting condition, noted. What is checked or written down when a unit leaves for site?
The driver just loads it. Sometimes a delivery note.
Noted, mostly no check at dispatch. Roughly how many units do you have out on hire in a typical month?
Thanks, noted — around 25 of 40 on hire. When a unit comes back, who receives it at the yard?
